marks.named: a Frogger/Freeway-style lane-crossing grid game (stated as best guess)
deductions: "Tile 3 is a wall/padding tile... It fills a fixed border (rows 0, 1, 9 and columns 0, 9)" and "Channel 2 never occurs anywhere" - row 1 is the goal row (channel 2), not part of the border; the reply misses the goal channel and folds the goal row into the border
"the channels behave like a one-hot cell type" / "input is... each cell one-hot encoded over 5 tile types" - channels are overlapping binary planes, not one-hot
marks.conclusion: A 10x10x5 grid-world input with a wall border and periodic row patterns; 5 outputs probably actions; best guess a Frogger-like lane game, but channels and outputs not assigned.
marks.judge_notes: Core 6 - 2 = 4. Border credited (the always-on set was found correctly) although goal row was merged into it and counted as channel 3. Channel meanings: only channel 3 (obstacles/wall) credited; ch0 agent / ch1 deadly obstacle / ch4 second object were in a hypothesis the reply labels 'plausible, not proven', so no credit. Layout 1 of 2: interior 7x8 region, ch1 absent from row 8, ch1 in rows 2-7 supported; agent location only hedged. B 0: 'no-op plus 4 moves' only appears inside the hedged hypothesis, and the reply says output meanings are inferred, not observed. Activation: 'presumably ReLU' as default = 0, and wrong but hedged so no deduction. Name bonus: the reply's best explanation is 'a lane/obstacle game... Frogger-like policy', flagged as its best guess; rubric does not say whether a flagged best guess counts as naming, I awarded the 2 bonus points since it commits to it as its concrete reading in section 7. Reply is cut off by nothing; complete.
